reviewed_sources.scope: Read the complete producer, including checkpoint reconstruction, all-five admission, state injection, observation masks, guard retention and failure persistence.

Focused reading of input_rows, readout, metric_arrays, common_schema, gate_schema, trajectory_schema, gate_recount, perturbation, null_number, censor_recount, event_audit and run. Not a complete independent review of every IO/helper routine.
Read the complete JavaScript source. No function invocation or numerical execution.
Read the native JSON/NPZ inventory, tensor comparison loop and final receipt fields to check the JavaScript inventory contract. This focused pass is not a complete binder review.

checks_by_inspection: All five 64-row compatibility evaluations and a durable summary precede every extended trajectory. The admitted condition uses finite values, absolute tolerance 1e-4 plus relative tolerance 1e-5, and exactly matching 64 predictions. A complete negative gate retains all five checks and creates no continuation directory.
The selected four states originate from the same 64-example T16 gate forward. They are not reconstructed by a separate four-example inference or treated as historically archived hidden states.

Checkpoint configuration, architecture, source and input hash links are checked before use. Strict state-dictionary loading and reconstructed zero nonpersistent buffers match the stated grounding-free setup.

The perturbation uses the literal channel/row/column checkerboard, float64 RMS-based nominal amplitude and float32 represented initial state. Its denominator is the positive finite RMS of the actual represented difference.

Each branch installs its initial state after the first discarded native update, then retains times 0 through 256. The original canvas remains available on every subsequent update, and evaluation disables stochastic firing.

The producer preserves the first nonfinite or finite cap-crossing state before stopping that branch. Unobserved states/logits use NaN padding and explicit masks. Readout finiteness is separate from state finiteness.
State L2/RMS/maxabs, adjacent-step L2 increments, centered float64 NLL, actual perturbation and common-observed-finite pair gains are consistent between the inspected producer and auditor routines.

The censor recount includes the first finite cap crossing in the observed finite domain, excludes a nonfinite endpoint from finite metrics, and does not convert missing endpoints to zero gain. Operational failures are not certified as completed trajectories.

The fresh-process controller orders recovery, native production, checkpoint binding and NumPy audit. It preserves component logs/status, uses disjoint receipt names and enforces the shared 600-second stage admission together with component limits.

The elementary JavaScript checks JSON arithmetic and cross-file counts only. Its binding inventory of 12 or 22 JSON/NPZ files correctly excludes events.jsonl, which is covered by the separate array-auditor native-tree/event checks.
interpretation_limits: The upper inventory is 40 trajectories and 20 directional pairs across five historical checkpoints and four correlated queries of one exposed validation scene; it is not 40 independent experiments or a new held-out generalization assay.
Compatibility concerns saved T16 outputs under a changed Python/thread runtime. It does not prove identity of historical hidden states or all subsequent states.
The fixed perturbation does not estimate an operator norm, worst-case sensitivity, Lyapunov exponent or global/infinite-time stability certificate.
The state cap and resource limits are operational guards. A cap crossing is a finite recorded event, not by itself an asymptotic-divergence proof.

The checkpoint binder checks saved parameter identity without inference; the NumPy auditor checks saved arrays, readouts and summaries without replaying recurrent dynamics. Neither is an external laboratory replication.
Low historical competence limits useful-memory interpretation but does not preclude descriptive state measurements. No claim about the cause of historical task failure is established here.
provenance_note: Candidate blobs were read before the item15B execution freeze. Listed SHA-256 values are the supplied candidate anchors; this static review did not independently hash them. The only authorized write for delivery is this unreferenced UTF-8 receipt blob.
